messages.author: f06db63329fab1f9
messages.subject: Re: Installing R packages
parts:
Hi Tomas, Olivier,

Yes-- in principle. 
But there are a bunch of caveats for the moment. 

First, install.packages() doesn't work due to some bug in Renjin affecting the install.packages() code. 
Second, support for native libraries is not finished yet, so if the packages relies on C / Fortran code, it probably won't work out of the box. (This will be finished by the end of the year I hope)

I haven't had time to experiment with bioconductor, but I suspect it will take some tinkering to get running properly.

To get external packages working with renjin today, the easiest way is to install them with C-R 2.x and then reference their path in your call to library. For example:

library('survey', lib.loc='/home/alex/R/library')

Note that Renjin does not and probably won't ever support R bytecode, so make sure to install the packages with <= R2.12 or disable compilation when installing.   

Unfortunately I just haven't had much time to make this easier -- at bedatadriven we use renjin for building webapps with R so we just stick the packages we need in a jar, and then place the jar on the classpath. 

Best,
Alex

messages.subject: Re: Installing R packages
parts:
Hi Angelo,
At present, we're reusing all of the original R package loading code, so the package has to be available somewhere where the R scripts can find it. We used to scan the whole classpath for packages, but this led to unacceptable loading times.

The only trick is that the packages have to be in the "packaged" format that these scripts expect, for example:

/home/alex/R-libs/bbmle/NAMESPACE
/home/alex/R-libs/bbmle/DESCRIPTION
/home/alex/R-libs/bbmle/Meta/package.rds
/home/alex/R-libs/bbmle/R/stats  (all R sources concatenated)

You can then load these packages by calling 

library("bbmle", lib.loc="/home/alex/R-libs")

In our webapps, we add all the jars in the WEB-INF/packages to the R library path when creating the R environment, so that scripts can just call library("bbmle") or bbmle::method to use the packages.

What renjin lacks now is an easy way to assemble package sources into the format expected by R. That's been on my list for a long time, so your question comes at the right moment and I'm devoting today to that. So I'll let you know later today how to generate the jars from R source packages. In the meantime, you can look at the Bootstrapper class in renjin-core to see how we assemble the builtin R packages like stats and tools.

Best,
Alex

Hi Angelo,
At present, we're reusing all of the original R package loading code, so the package has to be available somewhere where the R scripts can find it. We used to scan the whole classpath for packages, but this led to unacceptable loading times.

library("bbmle", lib.loc="/home/alex/R-libs")

What renjin lacks now is an easy way to assemble package sources into the format expected by R. That's been on my list for a long time, so your question comes at the right moment and I'm devoting today to that. So I'll let you know later today how to generate the jars from R source packages. Hi Angelo,
At present, we're reusing all of the original R package loading code, so the package has to be available somewhere where the R scripts can find it. We used to scan the whole classpath for packages, but this led to unacceptable loading times.

The only trick is that the packages have to be in the "packaged" format that these scripts expect, for example:

/home/alex/R-libs/bbmle/NAMESPACE
/home/alex/R-libs/bbmle/DESCRIPTION
/home/alex/R-libs/bbmle/Meta/package.rds
/home/alex/R-libs/bbmle/R/stats  (all R sources concatenated)

You can then load these packages by calling 

library("bbmle", lib.loc="/home/alex/R-libs")

In our webapps, we add all the jars in the WEB-INF/packages to the R library path when creating the R environment, so that scripts can just call library("bbmle") or bbmle::method to use the packages.

What renjin lacks now is an easy way to assemble package sources into the format expected by R. That's been on my list for a long time, so your question comes at the right moment and I'm devoting today to that. So I'll let you know later today how to generate the jars from R source packages. In the meantime, you can look at the Bootstrapper class in renjin-core to see how we assemble the builtin R packages like stats and tools.

Best,
Alex

Hi Angelo,
At present, we're reusing all of the original R package loading code, so the package has to be available somewhere where the R scripts can find it. We used to scan the whole classpath for packages, but this led to unacceptable loading times.

The only trick is that the packages have to be in the "packaged" format that these scripts expect, for example:

/home/alex/R-libs/bbmle/NAMESPACE
/home/alex/R-libs/bbmle/DESCRIPTION
/home/alex/R-libs/bbmle/Meta/package.rds
/home/alex/R-libs/bbmle/R/stats  (all R sources concatenated)

You can then load these packages by calling 

library("bbmle", lib.loc="/home/alex/R-libs")

In our webapps, we add all the jars in the WEB-INF/packages to the R library path when creating the R environment, so that scripts can just call library("bbmle") or bbmle::method to use the packages.

What renjin lacks now is an easy way to assemble package sources into the format expected by R. That's been on my list for a long time, so your question comes at the right moment and I'm devoting today to that. So I'll let you know later today how to generate the jars from R source packages. In the meantime, you can look at the Bootstrapper class in renjin-core to see how we assemble the builtin R packages like stats and tools.

Best,
Alex

Hi Tomas, Olivier,

Yes-- in principle. 
But there are a bunch of caveats for the moment. 

First, install.packages() doesn't work due to some bug in Renjin affecting the install.packages() code. 
Second, support for native libraries is not finished yet, so if the packages relies on C / Fortran code, it probably won't work out of the box. (This will be finished by the end of the year I hope)

I haven't had time to experiment with bioconductor, but I suspect it will take some tinkering to get running properly.

To get external packages working with renjin today, the easiest way is to install them with C-R 2.x and then reference their path in your call to library. For example:

library('survey', lib.loc='/home/alex/R/library')

Note that Renjin does not and probably won't ever support R bytecode, so make sure to install the packages with <= R2.12 or disable compilation when installing.   

Unfortunately I just haven't had much time to make this easier -- at bedatadriven we use renjin for building webapps with R so we just stick the packages we need in a jar, and then place the jar on the classpath.

Alex

Hi Angelo,
At present, we're reusing all of the original R package loading code, so the package has to be available somewhere where the R scripts can find it. We used to scan the whole classpath for packages, but this led to unacceptable loading times.

The only trick is that the packages have to be in the "packaged" format that these scripts expect, for example:

/home/alex/R-libs/bbmle/NAMESPACE
/home/alex/R-libs/bbmle/DESCRIPTION
/home/alex/R-libs/bbmle/Meta/package.rds
/home/alex/R-libs/bbmle/R/stats  (all R sources concatenated)

You can then load these packages by calling 

library("bbmle", lib.loc="/home/alex/R-libs")

In our webapps, we add all the jars in the WEB-INF/packages to the R library path when creating the R environment, so that scripts can just call library("bbmle") or bbmle::method to use the packages.

What renjin lacks now is an easy way to assemble package sources into the format expected by R. That's been on my list for a long time, so your question comes at the right moment and I'm devoting today to that. So I'll let you know later today how to generate the jars from R source packages. In the meantime, you can look at the Bootstrapper class in renjin-core to see how we assemble the builtin R packages like stats and tools.

Best,
Alex

Hi Tomas, Olivier,

Yes-- in principle. 
But there are a bunch of caveats for the moment. 

First, install.packages() doesn't work due to some bug in Renjin affecting the install.packages() code. 
Second, support for native libraries is not finished yet, so if the packages relies on C / Fortran code, it probably won't work out of the box. (This will be finished by the end of the year I hope)

I haven't had time to experiment with bioconductor, but I suspect it will take some tinkering to get running properly.

To get external packages working with renjin today, the easiest way is to install them with C-R 2.x and then reference their path in your call to library. For example:

library('survey', lib.loc='/home/alex/R/library')

Note that Renjin does not and probably won't ever support R bytecode, so make sure to install the packages with <= R2.12 or disable compilation when installing.   

Unfortunately I just haven't had much time to make this easier -- at bedatadriven we use renjin for building webapps with R so we just stick the packages we need in a jar, and then place the jar on the classpath. 

Best,
Alex

library('survey', lib.loc='/home/alex/R/library')

At present, we're reusing all of the original R package loading code, so the package has to be available somewhere where the R scripts can find it. We used to scan the whole classpath for packages, but this led to unacceptable loading times.

The only trick is that the packages have to be in the "packaged" format that these scripts expect, for example:

/home/alex/R-libs/bbmle/NAMESPACE
/home/alex/R-libs/bbmle/DESCRIPTION
/home/alex/R-libs/bbmle/Meta/package.rds
/home/alex/R-libs/bbmle/R/stats  (all R sources concatenated)

You can then load these packages by calling 

library("bbmle", lib.loc="/home/alex/R-libs")

In our webapps, we add all the jars in the WEB-INF/packages to the R library path when creating the R environment, so that scripts can just call library("bbmle") or bbmle::method to use the packages.

What renjin lacks now is an easy way to assemble package sources into the format expected by R. That's been on my list for a long time, so your question comes at the right moment and I'm devoting today to that. So I'll let you know later today how to generate the jars from R source packages. Hi Angelo,
At present, we're reusing all of the original R package loading code, so the package has to be available somewhere where the R scripts can find it. We used to scan the whole classpath for packages, but this led to unacceptable loading times.

The only trick is that the packages have to be in the "packaged" format that these scripts expect, for example:

/home/alex/R-libs/bbmle/NAMESPACE
/home/alex/R-libs/bbmle/DESCRIPTION
/home/alex/R-libs/bbmle/Meta/package.rds
/home/alex/R-libs/bbmle/R/stats  (all R sources concatenated)

You can then load these packages by calling 

library("bbmle", lib.loc="/home/alex/R-libs")

In our webapps, we add all the jars in the WEB-INF/packages to the R library path when creating the R environment, so that scripts can just call library("bbmle") or bbmle::method to use the packages.

What renjin lacks now is an easy way to assemble package sources into the format expected by R. That's been on my list for a long time, so your question comes at the right moment and I'm devoting today to that. So I'll let you know later today how to generate the jars from R source packages. In the meantime, you can look at the Bootstrapper class in renjin-core to see how we assemble the builtin R packages like stats and tools.

Il giorno lunedì 10 settembre 2012 17:31:43 UTC+2, Alexander Bertram ha scritto:
Hi Tomas, Olivier,

Yes-- in principle. 
But there are a bunch of caveats for the moment. 

First, install.packages() doesn't work due to some bug in Renjin affecting the install.packages() code. 
Second, support for native libraries is not finished yet, so if the packages relies on C / Fortran code, it probably won't work out of the box. (This will be finished by the end of the year I hope)

I haven't had time to experiment with bioconductor, but I suspect it will take some tinkering to get running properly.

To get external packages working with renjin today, the easiest way is to install them with C-R 2.x and then reference their path in your call to library. For example:

library('survey', lib.loc='/home/alex/R/library')

Note that Renjin does not and probably won't ever support R bytecode, so make sure to install the packages with <= R2.12 or disable compilation when installing.   

Unfortunately I just haven't had much time to make this easier -- at bedatadriven we use renjin for building webapps with R so we just stick the packages we need in a jar, and then place the jar on the classpath. 

Best,
Alex

Hi Angelo,
At present, we're reusing all of the original R package loading code, so the package has to be available somewhere where the R scripts can find it. We used to scan the whole classpath for packages, but this led to unacceptable loading times.

The only trick is that the packages have to be in the "packaged" format that these scripts expect, for example:

/home/alex/R-libs/bbmle/NAMESPACE
/home/alex/R-libs/bbmle/DESCRIPTION
/home/alex/R-libs/bbmle/Meta/package.rds
/home/alex/R-libs/bbmle/R/stats  (all R sources concatenated)

You can then load these packages by calling 

library("bbmle", lib.loc="/home/alex/R-libs")

In our webapps, we add all the jars in the WEB-INF/packages to the R library path when creating the R environment, so that scripts can just call library("bbmle") or bbmle::method to use the packages.

What renjin lacks now is an easy way to assemble package sources into the format expected by R. That's been on my list for a long time, so your question comes at the right moment and I'm devoting today to that. So I'll let you know later today how to generate the jars from R source packages. In the meantime, you can look at the Bootstrapper class in renjin-core to see how we assemble the builtin R packages like stats and tools.

Best,
Alex

Hi Tomas, Olivier,

Yes-- in principle. 
But there are a bunch of caveats for the moment. 

First, install.packages() doesn't work due to some bug in Renjin affecting the install.packages() code. 
Second, support for native libraries is not finished yet, so if the packages relies on C / Fortran code, it probably won't work out of the box. (This will be finished by the end of the year I hope)

I haven't had time to experiment with bioconductor, but I suspect it will take some tinkering to get running properly.

To get external packages working with renjin today, the easiest way is to install them with C-R 2.x and then reference their path in your call to library. For example:

library('survey', lib.loc='/home/alex/R/library')

Note that Renjin does not and probably won't ever support R bytecode, so make sure to install the packages with <= R2.12 or disable compilation when installing.   

Unfortunately I just haven't had much time to make this easier -- at bedatadriven we use renjin for building webapps with R so we just stick the packages we need in a jar, and then place the jar on the classpath. 

Best,
Alex
